title: SkipQ · live application demonstration
text: Skip Q is a food court ordering application with two roles: diner and stall vendor. This video records the running application, using seeded demonstration accounts and simulated payments. Browser actions are automated, and this voice is computer generated. I will follow one new order across both roles, demonstrate two checkout refusals, and show the supporting features and project evidence.

title: Diner · sign in
text: First, the diner signs in through the actual login form. The account enters the protected diner area. The vendor will use a separate browser session, so the two roles remain independent.

title: Diner · start with an empty cart
text: The test data includes a cart. I remove its existing lines through the interface, so the new order in this demonstration starts from an empty cart.

title: Diner · browse open stalls and available items
text: Only open stalls appear in the list. Charcoal Grill is open. Its menu shows prices, descriptions, and images. Pineapple Tart is already sold out, and its Add button is disabled.

title: Diner · add and review an item
text: I add one Charcoal Chicken Rice. The updated button confirms one is in the cart. The cart shows the item, quantity, and total of six dollars fifty. The server calculates this total.

title: Diner · genuine simulated-payment failure
text: Checkout offers Pay Now, Card, and Cashless simulations. I deliberately select the payment failure control. The application displays a real payment refusal, retains the cart, and allows a safe retry. This failure is kept in the recording.

title: Diner · retry successfully and receive a queue number
text: I turn the failure control off and retry on the same checkout screen. Payment succeeds, creating one order and a unique queue number. This number will identify the same order on both roles' screens.

title: Diner · track the new Pending order
text: The tracking screen shows Pending and the purchased item. It polls every three seconds for changes made by the vendor.

title: Vendor · sign in and locate the same order
text: Now the vendor signs in through the login form in an independent session. The paid order queue contains the exact queue number generated by the diner's checkout.

title: Vendor · accept the same order
text: The vendor opens that order and accepts it. Its status changes from Pending to Preparing. The screen offers only the next actions allowed by the server.

title: Diner · automatically observes Preparing
text: Back on the original tracking screen, the diner sees Preparing through its own polling. There is no manual refresh or replacement order.

title: Vendor · mark Ready
text: The vendor marks the order ready for collection. A no show is permitted only thirty minutes after the ready time. That action is unavailable for this newly ready order.

title: Diner · ready-for-collection notification
text: The diner sees the green collection banner after polling. It tells the diner to collect the order at the counter.

title: Vendor · mark Collected
text: The vendor marks the same order collected. It becomes final and read only. The diner also observes Collected, with the completion message.

title: Diner · current and past order history
text: The order list separates All, Current, and Past. The completed demonstration order is now in Past. An older seeded purchase still records Grilled Chicken Rice at six dollars, although today's menu uses a different name and price. History keeps the original purchase snapshot.

title: Rule violation 1 · load checkout while the item is available
text: For the first rule violation, I add an available Mango Sago and open checkout for two dollars fifty. I keep this checkout screen open while the vendor changes the item.

title: Before violation 1 · expected refusal
text: The rule is that an unavailable item cannot be ordered. Before paying, the vendor will mark this exact item sold out. I expect checkout to refuse it, name the unavailable item, retain the cart, and create no new order.

title: Vendor · mark Mango Sago sold out
text: The vendor marks Mango Sago sold out. The diner still has the checkout screen loaded from before that change. This is a genuine stale screen.

title: Diner · checkout visibly refuses the sold-out item
text: I press Pay on that existing screen. Checkout is refused and names Mango Sago. The cart remains available for review. A read only verification of the stored orders confirms no additional order was created.

title: Diner · cart retained and sold-out state visible
text: Reviewing the cart shows the same item with its sold out state. Known unavailable lines block checkout, while Remove remains available so the diner can recover.

title: Rule violation 2 · open a fresh checkout
text: I remove the sold out item, add one available Chicken Rice, and open checkout for six dollars fifty while the stall is still open.

title: Before violation 2 · expected refusal
text: The second rule is that a closed stall cannot accept a new order. Before paying, the vendor will close Charcoal Grill. I expect a visible checkout refusal, the cart retained, and no additional order. Existing paid orders must remain accessible.

title: Vendor · close the stall
text: The vendor closes the stall. The closed banner explains that new checkouts are refused and existing paid orders remain accessible.

title: Diner · checkout visibly refuses the closed stall
text: On the already open checkout, I press Pay. The application refuses the closed stall and explains when to try again. The cart still contains the Chicken Rice, and the stored order count is unchanged.

title: Vendor · add, edit and remove a menu item
text: I reopen the stall and restock Mango Sago. The vendor can also add a menu item, edit its price and description, then remove it. The form states its validation rules, and removal asks for confirmation. This temporary demonstration item is removed afterwards.

title: Vendor · reject a seeded Pending order and refund
text: This is a separate seeded Pending order, not the collected demonstration order. Rejecting it produces Cancelled and a refunded payment. The screen states the refund outcome before confirmation.

title: Vendor · an older seeded Ready order becomes NoShow
text: This separate seeded order has been ready for more than thirty minutes. The permitted no show action now appears. Confirming it produces No Show and keeps the payment paid. No timestamp is changed to bypass the rule.

title: Project evidence · actual retained verification results
text: The project uses React for the interface, Flask for the API, and Mongo D B for persistent data. The retained October seventh checks show three hundred thirteen unit tests passed, ten real database functional tests passed twice, and the assessed browser lifecycle passed twice. Production build and thirty layout captures were also checked. These are recorded results, not tests rerun during this video.

title: Performance evidence · measured local results and limits
text: The recorded load measurement used ten simulated users for two minutes: three hundred ninety five menu requests, zero failures, and a menu response ninety fifth percentile of twenty milliseconds. This is a small local seeded dataset on the development server. It does not establish production capacity or isolate database execution time.

title: Complete · same-order lifecycle and both rule refusals
text: This live recording showed diner and vendor sign in, one order through Pending, Preparing, Ready, and Collected, and both announced rule violations refused visibly. It also showed payment retry, history, menu management, refund, and no show. The video uses computer generated narration and automated browser actions. Review it before submission. Publishing, marker access, and submission remain separate steps.
